label: FY2027 Q2 (May–Jul 2026)
asOf: prices as of the 27 Oct 2026 close
headline: Up 23% in a day, driven by Claudeforce, not by growth

points.t: Revenue +11%, but the acquired Informatica contributed about 4.5 points; excluding it, about 6%.
Agentforce ARR above $1.5B, AI and data together about $3.9B; but the definition widened, so year-on-year isn't fully comparable.

points.b: EPS doubled mostly on one-offs and buybacks
points.t: $2.53 came from investment gains; the $25B buyback cut the share count by about 14%.

reaction: Stock: closed at $205.62 on report day and +22.6% ($252.05) the next day, on more than 3x normal volume. The main driver was Claudeforce, announced at the same time: Salesforce and Anthropic are putting CRM data and functions inside Claude, easing fears that “AI replaces SaaS”; the results themselves only beat slightly. Up another 1.6% on the third day. It closed at $240.89 on 27 Oct, 4.4% below the day after the report. The revenue estimate is the public consensus cited by Hudson Labs.

segments.title: By offering
segments.take: Growth came mainly from Data 360 and Platform, but most of that is the consolidated Informatica; core apps such as Sales and Service grew only about 8%.

rows.why: Includes about $440M of Informatica subscription revenue this quarter, Slack, MuleSoft and Data 360. About +6% excluding Informatica.
Sales, Service, Marketing, Commerce and other clouds, now all called Agentforce Applications. Marketing and Commerce remain weak.

segments.note: From FY27 Salesforce reports only two subscription categories and no longer breaks out Sales, Service and other clouds, so there are no five-quarter charts. Constant-currency growth: Applications +8%, Platform +20%.

extras.title: Where it sits in the AI loop
extras.take: Salesforce sits in the application layer at the end of the chain: whether enterprises pay for AI, and whether AI cuts software seats, shows up here. It chose to partner with Anthropic and put itself inside Claude.

items.w: Launched Claudeforce with Anthropic, putting CRM data and functions inside Claude; Slackbot also uses Claude. The stock rose 23% in a day on the news.
9 of the top 10 AI companies use Salesforce, with spending up 435% y/y.

Benioff said the company is “still stuck in some ways in the per-user model”. In late October ServiceNow fell 27% the next day and Microsoft's paid M365 seats grew only 5%: the market's worries about software haven't gone away.
An accelerated buyback funded with $25B of new bonds cut the share count by about 14%; operating cash flow growth guidance fell from 9–10% to 4–5% as a result.

extras.title: Where growth comes from
extras.take: Salesforce targets 10%+ organic growth a year, but organic growth is only about 6% now. The variables are whether AI products can pull growth back up, and whether AI agents replace seats.

items.w: Another 1,200 sellers by year end (about 15,000 today); whether paid seat counts fall is the most direct signal of AI disruption.
Only 5% of sales and service users have upgraded to premium editions; customers can pay per user, by usage or by outcome.
Agentforce ARR exceeds $1.5B (on a wider definition), with AI and data together about $3.9B; Claudeforce launched in September.

October 2025 investor day: FY30 revenue above $60B (excluding Informatica), 10%+ organic growth a year over FY26–FY30, and the “Rule of 50”. Organic growth this quarter was about 6%, well short of the target; management says it re-accelerates in the second half.
Watch for cRPO back below 12%, growth excluding acquisitions staying below 6%, falling paid seat counts, and Claudeforce's value staying mostly inside Claude.

extras.title: How much growth was bought
extras.take: Of the reported +11%, organic growth is about 6%; management says it re-accelerates in the second half.

items.w: Contributed $456M of revenue this quarter. Excluding it, revenue was about $10.89B, about +6.4% y/y. Q3 guidance includes slightly more than 4 points from Informatica.
$200M of the roughly $300M full-year revenue raise comes from these two acquisitions; no purchase prices disclosed.
Now includes AI features, Slackbot and Headless 360, a wider definition than last year. 2,000 new customers in paid production use this quarter, +70% q/q.
3.2B Agentic Work Units (a unit of work done by AI agents) this quarter; Slackbot users +150% q/q.

extras.title: One-offs in EPS
extras.take: EPS doubled y/y, but operations contributed little of it.

items.w: $2.61B of strategic investment gains, versus $6M a year ago. Non-GAAP EPS of $5.90 is about $3.37 excluding them.
$25B of bonds issued for an accelerated buyback; 103M shares delivered upfront at an average of about $176. The same profit is split across fewer shares.
Non-GAAP 34.1% versus 34.3% a year ago; GAAP 20.5% versus 22.8%.

trends.why: Highly seasonal; collections concentrate in Q4 and Q1

valuation.take: About 13x trailing free cash flow, a FCF yield of about 8%, its third lowest in five years (five-year median about 25x). At the median multiple, the current price needs free cash flow half of today's: the market is pricing AI disrupting software, not paying a premium for growth.

tiles.f: EV ≈ $224B (including about $31B of net debt) ÷ TTM revenue $43.9B

forward.title: The company already gives full-year EPS
steps: Q2's investment gain of about $2.53 won't repeat → about $14.16 excluding it
forward.note: Buybacks sharply reduce the share count, so EPS growth will clearly outpace net income growth. This is company guidance, not our forecast.

scenarios.note: Base is the FY27 guided revenue midpoint of about $46.25B; market cap about $193B. *Price: if the market pays the five-year median market cap / FCF of 24.9x, the current price needs only about $7.8B of annual free cash flow, about half of today's. The price is below the bear case, equivalent to assuming AI will clearly erode its cash flow. These assumptions are ours and are not forecasts.

history.title: Against its own last 5 years
history.sub: Market cap / free cash flow at quarter ends
history.note: About 13x now, above only 2 of the last 20 quarter ends (end of April and July 2026, about 10x), the 10th percentile. The multiple fell from 20x to 10x this year on fears that AI agents will reduce the number of software seats companies buy. GAAP profit swings with investment gains, so we use the FCF multiple. StockAnalysis data.

decomp.title: The +22.6% post-report move, decomposed
head: Measure
TTM free cash flow
Mkt cap/FCF
decomp.note: The new quarter replaces the one a year ago, and trailing free cash flow rose only 3.4%. Nearly all of the gain was a re-rating: the market is reassessing whether AI is a threat or an opportunity for Salesforce, with Claudeforce as the trigger.

cash.title: Buybacks and debt
cash.note: First-half buybacks of $27.3B exceeded the past year's total free cash flow, funded mainly by $25B of new bonds. That is why full-year operating cash flow growth guidance fell from 9–10% to 4–5% (higher interest). Capex is about 1.5% of revenue.

calc: Price $240.89: 27 Oct close; market cap ≈ $193B (about 800M shares from StockAnalysis market cap ÷ price), net debt about $31B, EV about $224B
Free cash flow = operating cash flow − capex: $2.18B + $5.32B + $6.56B + $1.10B = $15.15B
Around the report: price × 1.226, TTM free cash flow × 1.034 → multiple × 1.186
Scenario free cash flow = FY28 revenue × free cash flow margin

pricezone.sub: FY28 free cash flow (scenarios above) × our multiple ÷ about 800M shares; price at the 29 Oct close
pricezone.why: The price is at the top of the zone: buying now, the base case gains about 40% while the bear case loses about 17%, a reward/risk of about 2.3. The low end equals the bear-case price. The 10–18x multiples are all below its five-year median of about 25x because AI's impact on software is still unresolved; even so, the price is already close to the bear case.

changes.before: Agentforce is Salesforce's own AI agent platform.
changes.now: Launched Claudeforce with Anthropic, putting CRM inside Claude; Slackbot also uses Claude. Management calls it the “enterprise harness” (data, apps, agents and interface layers).

changes.before: Pushed per-user Agentforce editions and Flex credits.
changes.now: Customers can pay per user, by usage or by outcome; Benioff said the company is “still stuck in some ways in the per-user model”.
$46.1–46.4B, including $200M from the pending Contentful and Fin deals.
FY28 details deferred to the Dreamforce investor day.

digest.verdict: What the market rewarded was the Claudeforce story, not the results. Up 22.6% the next day, about 15 points ahead of the software ETF; after four weeks it was up 15.9%, still about 11 points ahead of IGV (+4.6%), though about 10% below its 3 Sep high of $264.43. Our points that four-tenths of growth was bought and that EPS doubled mainly on one-offs and buybacks didn't change the market's view: most of the re-rating from the AI partnership held, with only part of the initial excitement fading.
